intent: Authenticated customer asks the bank to arrange an £8,000 cash withdrawal today. He says it is for a "bank security collection", and an unidentified person beside him is coaching him to give a false reason.
summary: Do not arrange the £8,000 withdrawal. Hold it now and escalate the live call urgently to Brackenfold safeguarding/fraud support. The request matches a courier/safe-keeping scam: there is no verified security-collection instruction on record, and an unidentified person beside the caller told him to say it was for home renovations and is staying on the line. Also refer the case to the safeguarding specialist for possible coercion. Tell Ivo gently and briefly that the bank never collects cash for safe-keeping. Ask yes/no questions about whether he can speak privately.

facts.claim: Ivo Ternall passed the established phone authentication procedure and asked to arrange an £8,000 cash withdrawal today.
The customer said the cash is for a bank security collection: someone is coming to collect it so it can be kept safe.

An unidentified second voice, whose relationship to the customer is not verified, told the customer to say it is for home renovations, not to mention the collection, and that they will stay there while he speaks.
The account service record shows no verified security-collection instruction.
Safeguarding/fraud support is available to the case desk. Account restrictions require specialist authorisation. Customer information is restricted to the authenticated holder and recorded delegates.
The customer is pressing for the withdrawal to be arranged now and says the other person has to remain on the line.
No withdrawal arrangements have been made so far, and no desk response to the final request is recorded.
The call excerpt is a text transcript only; no audio is supplied.

missing: Identity of the second person and their relationship to the customer (not verified)
Whether the customer can speak freely and a safe way and time to contact him (no contact preference recorded in the supplied evidence)
Who contacted the customer about the claimed 'security collection', and how (not stated)
Whether any cash or other payments have already been handed over or sent (not stated)

steps.instruction: Do not arrange or schedule the £8,000 cash withdrawal requested by Ivo Ternall on 2026-11-12. Hold this request pending urgent fraud/safeguarding review. Reason: the stated purpose is a 'bank security collection' that has no verified record, and an unidentified person is coaching the customer to give a false reason. The hold covers this withdrawal request only. Do not place any wider account restriction from the case desk; that requires specialist authorisation.

rationale.explanation: The customer describes a courier/safe-keeping collection that the bank has no record of. A second voice told him to hide the real purpose. These are concrete scam and coercion warning signs attached to this specific cash withdrawal.
rationale.criterion: A suspected active scam or coercion requires holding the identified risky action; desk-level restriction of the wider account needs specialist authorisation.

steps.target: Brackenfold Bank case desk – £8,000 cash withdrawal request (case 024)

steps.instruction: Escalate urgently while the call is live, transferring or conferencing the customer if possible. Pass on the following: authenticated customer Ivo Ternall (passed phone authentication at 09:00 on 2026-11-12) requested an £8,000 cash withdrawal today for a 'bank security collection' where someone will collect the cash for safe-keeping; the account record shows no verified security-collection instruction; at 09:04 an unidentified voice beside the caller said 'Say it is for home renovations. Do not mention the collection. I will stay here while you speak'; at 09:06 the customer said that person has to remain on the line and pressed for the withdrawal now. Also pass on that the withdrawal is on hold at the desk, that no account restriction has been placed (specialist authorisation is needed), and that the call excerpt is text-only with no audio. Ask the specialist to decide on any account protection and on how to deal with the expected cash collection.

rationale.explanation: A cash collection may be imminent. The pattern matches an impersonation/courier scam, and the bank's directory shows safeguarding/fraud support is available to the case desk.
rationale.criterion: A suspected scam in progress requires urgent fraud/security escalation through a known bank route.

steps.instruction: Refer the case for safeguarding assessment of possible coercion, as part of the same handoff as s2. Pass on that an unverified person is physically present, is directing what the customer says, and insists on staying on the line. Note that no safe contact method or time is recorded. Any follow-up must use a route the customer himself confirms is safe, or a known bank route, and must not go through or be disclosed to the second person. Ask the specialist to establish safe contact with the customer.

rationale.explanation: The second voice is coaching the customer and refusing to leave, which points to possible coercion. The person's identity and relationship are unverified, so safe contact has not been established.
rationale.criterion: Coercion indicators require holding the unsafe action, protecting safe contact, avoiding disclosure to a possible controller and referring to a trained specialist.

steps.instruction: Speak calmly and briefly, with no blame and no account details, since another person may be listening. Say: 'Mr Ternall, I'm not able to arrange this cash withdrawal on this call. Brackenfold Bank never sends anyone to collect cash to keep it safe, and we have no record of any security collection on your account. Please don't hand cash to anyone who comes to collect it. I'm bringing in a specialist colleague now to help you. You can answer just yes or no: are you able to speak privately right now? Is there a safe number or time for us to reach you?' Do not ask for PINs, passwords or codes. Do not promise when the specialist will call back or what the outcome will be.

rationale.explanation: The customer needs to hear clearly that the bank does not collect cash, so he does not hand over money. Yes/no questions let him tell us about safety without alerting the person beside him.
rationale.criterion: Explain the hold and its reason without disclosing information to an unverified third party. Ask for a safe contact route without promising an outcome.

must_state: The bank will not arrange the £8,000 withdrawal on this call while a fraud/safeguarding specialist reviews it
Brackenfold Bank never sends anyone to collect cash for safe-keeping, and the bank has no record of any security collection on this account
Do not hand cash to anyone who comes to collect it
A specialist colleague is being brought in now. Do not say that contact has been made until it is confirmed
must_not: Arrange, schedule or facilitate the £8,000 cash withdrawal, or accept 'home renovations' as the reason
Ask for PINs, passwords, one-time codes or card details
Disclose account information, balances or case details to the unidentified second person, or ask that person to confirm anything
Use any contact details or callback route supplied by the second person or the claimed 'collector'
Claim that an account restriction has been placed; restrictions need specialist authorisation
Claim that the fraud/safeguarding team has already been contacted or has acted before this is confirmed
Promise reimbursement or recovery, or blame the customer
State as fact that the second person is a criminal or abuser; their identity and relationship are unverified
Send case summaries or alerts to a contact route not confirmed as safe by the customer
